headline: BWP Trust divesting former Bunnings sites and acquiring large format retail assets to enhance income growth for security holders.
reasoning: BWP Trust divested three former Bunnings sites, including one at Chadstone, where management felt the market valued the assets more than they did internally. The Chadstone asset had a shorter lease relative to the rest of the portfolio, and redevelopment risk on Bunnings vacating was a factor in the decision to sell. On the acquisition side, BWP added two large format retail assets — one in Queensland and one in Victoria — where management sees lease restructuring opportunities and income growth potential. Scatena expressed confidence in the portfolio's valuation, noting recent Bunnings-related transactions support tight yields in the sector. He highlighted strong capital flows into large format retail from both listed and unlisted REITs as supportive of current cap rates.
quote: Yeah. So typically we will look at assets all the time in terms of highest and best use, and a couple of those assets that we divested, or a number or the three assets we divested. They were former Bunnings sites and Bunnings had vacated and we had repurposed some of them in terms of retaining them. But we felt that the market perhaps valued those more than we did. Um, Chadstone being an example of an asset that we looked at. Bunnings is in that asset at the moment. It's a shorter lease relative to the other leases we have. Um, and we formed a view that, you know, the market perhaps valued that a little more than us. We look at redevelopment of that asset in the occasion, on the occasion that Bunnings would leave. But we felt divesting was in the interests of security holders. So we do that often on parts of the portfolio, and they generated very strong returns for security holders. Um, and in regards to inorganic acquisitions, yes, we're always looking at that. Very difficult to forecast. You know, we have a small team that is now dedicated to that task. And those two assets were large format retail assets, one in Queensland, one in Victoria. And those fundamentals that I mentioned before that were attracted to and also lease income growth opportunities. If we curate the lease structures there, we think there's good income growth for security holders over time.
